claims.text: The baseline AlCoFeNi alloy has a relatively homogeneous phase and lower coercivity.
The modified alloy has composition AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi.
AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi is produced from AlCoFeNi by substituting part of Fe with Cr.
Introducing Cr enhances phase separation in this alloy system.
AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi develops a hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure.
Disordered A2 precipitates are embedded in an ordered B2 matrix.
The B2 matrix is weakly ferromagnetic.
Localized magnetic vortex states form within individual A2 precipitates.
The coercivity of AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi originates in part from a complex magnetization process involving successive reversal of magnetic vortices.
The vortex states and associated magnetic nonuniformity act as pinning centers that impede domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion requires a larger applied field to reverse magnetization and therefore increases coercivity.
AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi will have a higher coercive field than matched AlCoFeNi.
The baseline AlCoFeNi alloy has a more homogeneous magnetic microstructure than AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi.
Conventional thermal processing allows the alloy to decompose naturally into A2 and B2 phases.
The proposed coercivity effect holds at ambient temperature without applying a magnetic field during processing.
The effect should apply near the AlCo(Fe,Cr)Ni compositional space under similar thermal conditions.
Applying a magnetic field during synthesis or using extreme Cr concentrations could produce alternative phases and magnetic behavior.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement depends strongly on the extent of hierarchical phase separation and processing details.
TEM and XRD can verify both the B2 + A2 hierarchy and the presence of magnetic vortex states.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as replacing Fe with Cr, but the formulas change AlCoFeNi to AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi: Fe remains at the same formula coefficient while Co decreases from 1 to 0.5 and Cr is added at 0.5. Thus, the stated formulas describe replacement of half of Co, not Fe.
